h1:
Ayutthaya Mookata & BBQ Buffet
10 Best Value Dinner Spots
intro: When the sun drops in Ayutthaya, the dinner locals reach for most often is mookata — Thai grill-and-hotpot — and Korean BBQ. You sit around the dome grill, dip everything in jaew, and talk for hours until the place closes. We picked 10 spots Ayutthaya locals actually eat at, from no-time-limit mookata buffets to riverside Korean BBQ, with rough prices and the area each one sits in, so you can choose by budget.

blocks.html: Mookata in Ayutthaya splits into two main camps. The first is the all-you-can-eat mookata buffet, where you sit at the grill and refill as much as you like — easy to keep the per-head cost in check and great for groups. The second is Korean BBQ, which leans on marinated cuts and a wider food line; it costs a bit more but the vibe is built for lingering, and a few spots even sit right by the water for a cool evening.

items.name: Tidman Buffet Hot-Pan BBQ, Ayutthaya Branch
items.blurb: All-you-can-eat mookata buffet with no time limit and a very low starting price. Sit at the grill and refill freely, with pork collar, pork belly, bacon, and beef to choose from. This is the first pick for anyone on a budget who just wants to eat their fill without holding back.
items.meta: Aiyakan night market, Khlong Suan Phlu · open 16:00–23:00 · no time limit

items.name: Ah-Pa Grilled Prawns, Rojana Ayutthaya
items.blurb: A grill buffet that stands out for seafood — prawns, crab, fish, and duck, all fresh and brought out in real quantity. Reviews say it's worth it if you come as a group and share the grilling. The price already includes drinks.
items.meta: Rojana area · no time limit · drinks included

items.name: Nai Na Mee Nuea Halal Grill Buffet
items.blurb: A halal grill buffet, which isn't easy to find in Ayutthaya. The price covers free drink refills, and it suits anyone who eats halal and wants a varied meat line. Dinner only.

items.name: Mata Mookata Buffet, Rojana Ayutthaya
items.blurb: A mookata buffet with a long seafood line and live music while you eat. The mood is lively and works well for big groups that want to settle in for the night. Reviews rate it highly for the range of ingredients.

items.name: Korean Sol
items.blurb: Korean BBQ buffet in the town center, focused on Korean-style marinated cuts — pork collar, pork belly, bacon, marinated pork, and marinated chicken. Capped at 1.5 hours, it suits anyone who likes a deep, marinated flavor.

items.name: Jane Mookata, Pratu Chai Branch
items.blurb: A mookata spot in the Pratu Chai area that locals nearby keep coming back to. The ingredient line is generous and the price is friendly — good for an easy dinner without driving far.

items.name: Rim Khlong Korean Grill, Ayutthaya
items.blurb: Korean BBQ served as sets, with seating right by the canal and a cool view in the evening. The per-set price is easy on the wallet, which suits couples or small groups who care more about the setting than eating endlessly.

items.name: O Korean Grilled
items.blurb: Korean BBQ sets at a modest price, with your pick of pork or beef. Reviews are fairly good for a small-set spot, and it suits anyone who wants to try Korean BBQ without committing to a full buffet.

items.name: Riverside Grill
items.blurb: The riverside mookata with the lowest starting price on this list. The draw is the house-made dipping sauce, plus a breezy seat by the water — good for anyone who wants an easy meal on a small budget with no rush.

items.name: The Cafe Mookata Ayutthaya
items.blurb: Cafe-style mookata — clean, fresh-looking, with a varied menu. It suits anyone who wants a comfier seat than the usual roadside mookata stall.

blocks.title: How to pick a spot
blocks.html: If you're coming as a big group and want to control the budget, go for a no-time-limit mookata buffet like Tidman or Ah-Pa — better value than the set-menu spots. But if you'd rather take it slow and not feel rushed, a riverside or cafe-style place lets you sit and linger longer.

blocks.text: All-you-can-eat buffet vs. set BBQ — how to choose

blocks.html: The two differ mainly in how you eat. A mookata buffet suits a hungry group that wants a fixed per-head cost — pay one price and refill all night. Set-menu Korean BBQ leans on quality marinated cuts in a portion that's just right, which suits couples or small groups who don't eat a lot but want a fuller flavor.

items: Big appetite, big group — go for a no-time-limit buffet, where the per-head cost is clear and you come out ahead of paying per set
Quality cuts — set-menu Korean BBQ gives you deeply marinated meat in a right-sized portion, with nothing left to waste
You want the setting — a riverside or cafe-style spot lets you sit and linger with no rush
Eating halal — Nai Na Mee Nuea is a halal grill buffet that's not easy to find in Ayutthaya

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Mookata spots open mainly for dinner, and prices can move up with ingredient costs. The prices listed here are rough figures from reviews, so check the restaurant's page again before you go. Some places have a fixed weekly closing day, and a few branches have switched from set menus to buffets, so it's worth calling to confirm if you're coming as a big group.

faq.q: Which mookata in Ayutthaya is the best value?
faq.a: By per-head price, Tidman Buffet BBQ at Khlong Suan Phlu starts around 199 THB with no time limit, making it the best pick for a hungry group on a budget. Riverside Grill starts at 99 THB if you want something lighter.

faq.q: Does Ayutthaya have a halal grill buffet?
faq.a: Yes — Nai Na Mee Nuea is a halal grill buffet at around 279 THB per person including free drink refills. It opens for dinner from 16:00–22:00 and is closed on Thursdays.

faq.q: What time do mookata spots in Ayutthaya open?
faq.a: Most are dinner places, open from late afternoon until late — roughly 16:00–22:00 or 23:00. Some have a fixed weekly closing day, so it's best to check the restaurant's page before you go.

faq.q: I want a riverside setting — which spot should I go to?
faq.a: Rim Khlong Korean Grill and Riverside Grill both let you sit by the water for a cool evening, which suits couples or small groups who want an easy, unhurried meal.

faq.q: What's the difference between an all-you-can-eat buffet and a set BBQ?
faq.a: With an all-you-can-eat buffet you pay one price and refill freely, which suits a hungry group. Set-menu Korean BBQ focuses on quality marinated cuts in a right-sized portion, better for small groups who don't eat a lot.
